blocks.text: Primary amenorrhoea refers to the absence of menstruation by the expected age of menarche.

rows: Normal physiological variation or constitutional delay

items.text: Normal variation: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty.
Ovarian failure: Turner syndrome (45,X), gonadal dysgenesis and premature ovarian insufficiency.
Pituitary disorders: Hypopituitarism, pituitary tumours and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.
Endocrine disorders: Hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism and hyperprolactinaemia.
Reproductive tract abnormalities: Müllerian agenesis (MRKH syndrome).
Imperforate hymen: Menstrual blood cannot escape despite normal hormonal function.
Outflow obstruction: Transverse vaginal septum and cervical agenesis.
Disorders of sexual development: Complete androgen insensitivity syndrome.

rows: Normal breasts, uterus present, cyclic pain

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Investigations include pregnancy testing, FSH, LH, prolactin, TSH, pelvic ultrasound and karyotyping when indicated.
Secondary amenorrhoea is the absence of menstruation for at least 3 months in someone with previously regular cycles, or 6 months in someone with previously irregular cycles.

rows: Reduced body weight or excessive exercise

items.text: Pregnancy: The commonest cause to exclude.
Reduced body weight: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhoea.
Excessive exercise: Suppression of hypothalamic GnRH secretion.
Anatomical abnormalities: Intrauterine adhesions following uterine instrumentation (Asherman syndrome).
Thyroid disorders: Both hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Always exclude pregnancy first, regardless of the patient's contraceptive history.
Abnormal uterine bleeding refers to bleeding that is abnormal in frequency, regularity, duration or volume.

items.text: Adenomyosis: Endometrial glands within the myometrium.
Ovulatory dysfunction: PCOS, thyroid disease and perimenopause.
Endometrial: Local abnormalities of endometrial haemostasis.
Iatrogenic: Hormonal contraceptives, anticoagulants and certain medications.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: PALM–COEIN is the FIGO classification for causes of abnormal uterine bleeding in non-pregnant women of reproductive age. Always exclude pregnancy-related bleeding separately.
Heavy menstrual bleeding is excessive menstrual blood loss that affects physical, emotional, social or material quality of life.
Examination pearl: Heavy menstrual bleeding is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Investigate according to age, pregnancy possibility, symptoms, examination and endometrial cancer risk.
Oligomenorrhoea refers to infrequent menstruation, commonly with menstrual cycles longer than 35 days.

items.text: R – Reduced ovarian reserve or premature ovarian insufficiency.

blocks.text: Most causes interfere with the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis, resulting in abnormal follicular development or ovulation.
Examination pearl: PCOS is an important cause of oligomenorrhoea. Consider hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology and ovulatory dysfunction when evaluating the patient.

items.text: I – Inflammatory pelvic disease and endometriosis.
N – Neoplasms and other pelvic pathology.

blocks.text: Painful menstruation without identifiable pelvic pathology.

items.text: Begins within a few years of menarche.
May radiate to the back and thighs.
Usually occurs around the onset of menstruation.

blocks.text: Painful menstruation associated with underlying pelvic disease.
Examination pearl: New-onset dysmenorrhoea, progressively worsening pain, dyspareunia or infertility should raise suspicion of secondary dysmenorrhoea.

Infertility is generally defined as failure to achieve pregnancy after 12 months of regular unprotected sexual intercourse. Earlier evaluation is appropriate in older women and those with known risk factors.

items.text: Standard investigations do not identify a cause.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Always investigate both partners rather than automatically attributing infertility to the woman.
Examination pearl: Ovulatory dysfunction, particularly PCOS, is a major cause of female infertility. Tubal disease is especially important where untreated pelvic infections are common.

items.text: Sperm production: Testicular failure, cryptorchidism, varicocele, genetic disorders and gonadotoxic treatments.
Transport: Epididymal or vas deferens obstruction, congenital absence of vas deferens.
Endocrine: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, hyperprolactinaemia and pituitary disease.
Infections: Epididymo-orchitis and certain sexually transmitted infections.
Mechanical: Erectile dysfunction, ejaculatory disorders and anatomical abnormalities.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Semen analysis is a first-line investigation. Abnormal results generally require confirmation with repeat testing and further assessment.

rows: No offensive smell or significant irritation

items.text: I – Infection with other sexually transmitted organisms.
N – Neoplasia of cervix or vagina.
L – Local irritation, foreign bodies and other causes.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Vaginal discharge is not always due to an STI. History, examination, pH testing, microscopy and appropriate molecular tests help establish the diagnosis.
PID is an infection and inflammation of the upper female genital tract.

items.text: Recent uterine instrumentation in selected circumstances.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: A low threshold for empirical treatment is recommended when clinical suspicion is present. Do not delay treatment while awaiting test results.
Chronic pelvic pain is persistent or recurrent pelvic pain, commonly lasting at least six months, although definitions vary.
Examination pearl: Chronic pelvic pain is frequently multifactorial. A patient may have coexisting gynaecological, gastrointestinal, urinary and musculoskeletal disorders.

items.text: I – Inflammatory or tubo-ovarian cystic masses.
L – Luteinised cysts associated with pregnancy or hormonal stimulation.
E – Ectopic pregnancy-related adnexal mass (important differential, not a true ovarian cyst).
Acute pain if torsion or rupture occurs.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Transvaginal ultrasound is a key initial investigation. Management depends on symptoms, age, menopausal status, cyst appearance and malignancy risk.
Ovarian torsion is twisting of the ovary, sometimes involving the fallopian tube, around its supporting ligamentous structures, compromising venous and eventually arterial blood flow.

items.text: S – Stimulation of ovaries during fertility treatment.
T – Twisting of the ovarian pedicle.
Ovarian masses, particularly those measuring approximately 5 cm or larger.
Sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain.
Intermittent episodes of pain due to torsion and detorsion.
Doppler assessment of ovarian blood flow.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Normal Doppler blood flow does NOT exclude ovarian torsion. It is a surgical emergency requiring urgent gynaecological assessment and usually laparoscopy.
Uterine fibroids (leiomyomas) are benign monoclonal tumours arising from uterine smooth muscle.

items.text: Fibroids originate from individual myometrial smooth muscle cells.
MED12 mutations and other molecular abnormalities are implicated.
Extracellular matrix accumulation contributes to tumour development.

rows: Beneath endometrium, projecting into uterine cavity

items.text: Infertility or adverse reproductive outcomes in selected cases.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Submucosal fibroids are particularly associated with heavy menstrual bleeding and impaired fertility.
Endometriosis is a chronic inflammatory condition characterised by endometrial-like tissue outside the uterine cavity.
Examination pearl: Endometriosis is not diagnosed solely by the presence of visible lesions. Normal pelvic examination or ultrasound does not exclude superficial disease.
Adenomyosis occurs when endometrial glands and stroma are present within the myometrium, often accompanied by hypertrophy of surrounding smooth muscle.

items.text: Y – Years of reproductive hormonal exposure.
O – Obstetric or uterine instrumentation associations.

subsections.subsection_title: 18. Causes and risk factors for cervical cancer

blocks.text: Cervical cancer is a malignant tumour arising from the cervix, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection being the central causal factor in nearly all cases.

rows: Vulnerability due to immunosuppression, including HIV

blocks.text: Important clarification: Persistent infection with oncogenic HPV types, especially HPV 16 and 18, is the principal cause. Other listed factors modify risk rather than independently causing cervical cancer.

items.text: Advanced disease: urinary obstruction, rectal symptoms and weight loss.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: HPV vaccination is preventive, not therapeutic. It does not eliminate the need for cervical screening.
Endometrial cancer is a malignant tumour of the uterine endometrium.
The major concept is prolonged exposure to oestrogen without adequate progesterone opposition.

rows: Mismatch repair gene mutations – Lynch syndrome

items.text: Hypertension, often associated with metabolic risk factors.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Postmenopausal bleeding must always be investigated. Transvaginal ultrasound and endometrial sampling are important diagnostic tools.
Ovarian cancer includes several different tumour types, with epithelial ovarian cancer being the commonest group.

rows: Reproductive factors – nulliparity and infertility associations

items.text: Strong family history of ovarian or breast cancer.
Endometriosis, particularly for clear cell and endometrioid ovarian cancers.
Risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy in appropriately selected high-risk individuals.
L – Lower abdominal or pelvic pain.
A – Appetite changes or early satiety.
T – Toilet symptoms: urinary urgency or frequency.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Ovarian cancer often presents late because early symptoms are vague and non-specific. CA-125 is not a screening test for average-risk asymptomatic women.
Pelvic organ prolapse occurs when pelvic organs descend into or through the vaginal canal due to weakness or damage to pelvic support structures.
Examination pearl: The POP-Q system is used for objective staging of pelvic organ prolapse.
Urinary incontinence is the involuntary leakage of urine.
Leakage associated with a sudden compelling desire to urinate.
Leakage due to incomplete bladder emptying.
The urinary system may function adequately, but physical, cognitive or environmental limitations prevent timely toileting.
Features of both stress and urge incontinence.

blocks.title: A useful mnemonic for reversible contributors to incontinence, especially in older patients:

rows: Pills, implants, injectables, patch, vaginal ring

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Condoms provide protection against many sexually transmitted infections, unlike hormonal contraceptives and intrauterine methods.
Contraindications differ according to the contraceptive method. The WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria and CDC Medical Eligibility Criteria provide standard guidance.

items.text: S – Severe hypertension and vascular disease.
A – Active or previous thromboembolic disease.
F – Female-specific cancers and significant liver disease.
E – Early postpartum period and other method-specific risks.

rows: Early postpartum period, depending on breastfeeding and VTE risk
Risk of severe hypertension or vascular complications
Greater age with smoking, especially age 35 or above

blocks.text: Generally suitable for many women who cannot use oestrogen.
Examination pearl: Do not treat every contraindication as absolute. Medical eligibility categories are:
Menopause is defined retrospectively after 12 consecutive months without menstruation, when there is no other pathological or physiological explanation.

items.text: Loss of negative feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary axis.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Menopause is usually a clinical diagnosis in women aged 45 years and above with typical symptoms. Routine FSH testing is generally unnecessary in this age group.

items.text: Increased insulin resistance in some women.
Cardiovascular risk rises with age and other risk factors.
Pelvic organ prolapse may become more symptomatic.

blocks.text: Examination pearl: Menopause does not directly cause all cardiovascular disease or cognitive decline. Ageing, lifestyle, genetics and associated metabolic factors contribute significantly.
